title: Everyone's brain is different, and that is great
examples: Why is school easy for some kids and hard for me?

explain.say: Here is a question. Are all brains the same? No. Every brain is a little different. Look at the board. Here are two friends, Priya and Kofi. The board shows what each one is good at.

draw.text: Everyone's brain is different, and that is great

explain.say: Look at Priya's side. She is great at drawing. She remembers pictures easily. Spelling feels hard for her. She learns spellings with pictures to help. What is easy for you?
Now look at Kofi's side. He is great at numbers, and he loves facts. Sitting still for a long time feels hard for him. Movement breaks help him learn. Is there something that feels hard for you?

People can be good at many kinds of things. Making things, like drawing and cooking. Thinking, like numbers and puzzles. People, like kindness and jokes. Moving, like dancing and sport. Which group has something you are good at?
Priya and Kofi are different, and both are great. The world needs all kinds of people. That includes you. Today, tell a grown-up one thing you are good at.

faq.a: Every brain is a little different. Everyone learns in their own way. Most people learn best when they see it, hear it and do it.

faq.q: What does Priya's brain find easy?
faq.a: Priya is great at drawing and remembering pictures. Spelling is trickier, so she uses pictures to help her learn words.

faq.q: What does Kofi's brain find easy?
faq.a: Kofi is great at numbers and facts. He learns best when he can take movement breaks.

faq.q: Is it okay to find some things hard?
faq.a: Yes. Everyone finds some things hard. Hard means you need a different way, or more practice. A grown-up you trust can help.
asks: Some things are hard for me

faq.q: What can brains be great at?
faq.a: Making things, thinking, people skills, moving and much more. Most brains are great at several things.

facts: Neurodiversity is the idea that brains naturally differ, and that these differences are part of human variety.
No two brains are exactly the same.

quiz.say: Priya is great at drawing. Kofi is great at numbers. What does this show?
quiz.show: Priya: drawing. Kofi: numbers. What does this show?

options.show: Everyone is good at different things
options.say: Everyone is good at different things

options.show: Only one of them is clever
options.say: Only one of them is clever

quiz.why: Priya and Kofi have different strengths. Both of them are clever in their own way.

wrong.1: Both of them are clever, in different ways.
wrong.2: Drawing and numbers are both useful things to be good at.

quiz.say: Spelling feels hard for Priya. She is great at drawing. What can help her?
quiz.show: Spelling is hard for Priya. What can help?
quiz.why: Priya remembers pictures well. A picture beside each word helps her learn it.

wrong.0: Priya can learn spellings when she has the right help.
wrong.1: Hurrying makes hard work harder, so slow practice is better.
